subject.title: [Bug]: `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` breaks `openai-codex` auth/keychain paths on macOS and can fail fresh runtime launch with `SecItemCopyMatching failed -50`

question: For macOS, should OpenClaw preserve the `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` launchd default and isolate Codex/OpenAI keychain auth reads from it, or change the global service TLS default?
rationale: Both sides protect real behavior: the current default supports launchd TLS, while the reported failure affects auth/keychain and fresh runtime launch paths, so an automated patch should not choose the product/security boundary without maintainer intent and live macOS proof.

options.title: Scope auth/keychain boundary
options.body: Keep the launchd TLS default and make Codex/OpenAI auth/status/app-server launch paths use a keychain-safe, non-prompting boundary with live macOS verification.

options.title: Change global macOS TLS default
options.body: Disable or reverse the macOS `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA` default, accepting the risk of reintroducing launchd TLS failures unless broad macOS service proof covers it.

options.title: Pursue credential delegation
options.body: Treat the external delegation idea as a larger auth architecture change only if maintainers want that product direction and can own its security model.

recommendation.title: Scope auth/keychain boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the launchd TLS default and make Codex/OpenAI auth/status/app-server launch paths use a keychain-safe, non-prompting boundary with live macOS verification.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest shared history across both sides of the boundary: Codex Keychain credential reads and centralized Node startup TLS planning.
